title: Vibrato and telling Black and white trumpeters apart
summary: On returning from Europe he found everyone playing straight tone, so he could no longer tell Black from white players by vibrato.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: See, what happens... Let me explain something to you, what happened. When I left here, the trumpet players that were of any note had their own individual sound. You could tell Louis if you heard him, you could tell Cootie if you heard him -- right? You could tell Bobby Starks if you heard him. You could tell Red Allen if you heard him. You could tell Lips Page. Any of those cats that were like the big cats of the day, they had their own distinct sound. And they all had some kind of vibrato, you know.

Now, when I come back from Europe, everybody's playing straight tone. No vibrato at all. So that makes everybody sound alike. Right? So you can't tell who's playing. And they're also playing all of the same riffs together that...the same ones all the cats play, right? So how in the hell are you going to tell what's Black or White? The only way I could tell before is because most of the Black cats used lip vibrato, you know, and most White cats did this.
